manifest.scope: Section 10.1 Credit Card Processing Requirements, subsections 10.1.1-10.1.8

reviewPolicy.dataPolicy: TD files are fixture-design placeholders, not converter-ready requests; no response/host oracle is invented.
reviewPolicy.matchPolicy: Existing rules are references only. No AI/Test semantic crosswalk or coverage credit is asserted.
reviewPolicy.promotionGate: Authorized Test Solution review must approve BR wording/source applicability and complete real TD/request/response oracles before execution readiness.

businessRequirements.title: Credit card expiration date is validated
businessRequirements.requirement: For a credit-card transaction, the device validates the expiration date of the presented card.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: The device performs expiration date validation in a credit card transaction.

businessRequirements.title: Track selection uses the supported default and fallback
businessRequirements.requirement: When Track 2 is supported, the device sends Track 2 by default; if it cannot read Track 2, it sends unaltered Track 1 before manual entry, subject to the Amex-specific rule.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: The default track that is sent to the host should be Track 2 if the device supports Track 2.

businessRequirements.title: American Express track selection uses Track 1 first
businessRequirements.requirement: For American Express, the device sends Track 1 by default and sends unaltered Track 2 before manual entry when Track 1 cannot be read.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: For American Express, the default track should be Track 1.

businessRequirements.title: Encrypted AFD Track 1 data is carried in its encryption block
businessRequirements.requirement: For an AFD transaction with encrypted TransArmor data, Track 1 is present in the Encryption Block and the Encryption Target identifies Track 1.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: If the AFD transaction being submitted contains encrypted data in the TransArmor Encryption Block, Track 1 data must be present inside the Encryption Block with Encryption Target as Track 1.

businessRequirements.title: Offline pre-authorization and sale preserve full track data
businessRequirements.requirement: An offline-approved Pre-Auth or Sale sends full track data; follow-up transactions use truncated Track 2 or truncated Track 2 facsimile.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: If a Pre-Auth transaction is approved offline, the full track data must be sent. Also if a Sale transaction is approved offline, the full track data must be sent.

businessRequirements.title: Manual entry follows three unsuccessful magnetic-stripe attempts
businessRequirements.requirement: After three unsuccessful magnetic-stripe reads, the device prompts for manual Account Number and Expiration Date in MMYY format.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: If unable to read the magnetic strip after three attempts, the device should prompt for manual entry of the Account Number and Expiration Date (Format:  MMYY).

businessRequirements.title: Manual entry is identified on receipt and journal
businessRequirements.requirement: When manual entry is used, an asterisk precedes the Account Number on the receipt and journal.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: If manual entry is used, this fact is indicated on the receipt and journal by an asterisk (*) before the Account Number.

businessRequirements.title: POS credit-card processing supports the documented transaction set
businessRequirements.requirement: Point-of-sale credit processing supports the transaction types enumerated in Section 10.1.2, including purchase/capture, reversal, authorization-only, return, timeout reversal, mail/phone, void, balance inquiry, partial approval, and authorization-only reversal.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: The following point-of-sale transactions are supported for credit card processing:

businessRequirements.title: Customer-activated credit processing supports its documented transaction set
businessRequirements.requirement: Customer-activated credit processing supports Purchase/Capture, Authorization Only, Time-out Reversal, Partial Approval, and Authorization Only Reversal.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: The following customer-activated transactions are supported for credit card processing:

businessRequirements.title: Partial approval response identifies the approved amount and remaining balance
businessRequirements.requirement: With Partial Approval Indicator 1, the network response uses Response Code F, provides the approved amount, and prompts payment of the remaining balance; issuer-returned balance is carried in Segment 112.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: A Response Code (Element No. 83) value of F (Indicates “approval, partial amount approved.”)

businessRequirements.title: Partial approval applies only to the documented POS and CAT transaction contexts
businessRequirements.requirement: Partial Approval is supported for POS Purchase, POS Authorization Only, and CAT Authorization Only.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: Partial Approval transactions are supported for:

businessRequirements.title: Partial-approval reversal uses the approved amount and is not a partial reversal
businessRequirements.requirement: A reversal of a partially approved authorization uses the amount approved in the original response; BUYPASS supports reversal of the partially approved authorization, not a partial reversal of an original transaction.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: The amount in a Reversal (Void) request must be the amount approved in the original transaction response when a transaction has been partially approved.

businessRequirements.title: Partial-approval timeout reversal preserves original requested amount and sequence
businessRequirements.requirement: For a partially approved transaction, the TOR uses the amount requested in the original request and the original request's Sequence Number.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: The amount in a TOR request must be the amount requested in the original transaction response when a transaction has been partially approved.

businessRequirements.title: Approved authorizations are cleared or reversed within applicable timeframes
businessRequirements.requirement: Approved and partially approved authorizations are cleared or reversed; the source gives separate 24-hour card-present and 72-hour card-absent merchant windows.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: All approved and partially approved authorization transactions must be either cleared or reversed.

businessRequirements.title: Issuer processes matched authorization reversals and releases applicable holds
businessRequirements.requirement: The issuer immediately processes a matched reversal subject to its risk/fraud controls and releases any applicable hold on cardholder available funds; issuer processing requires independent host/issuer evidence.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: Issuers must immediately process matched reversal transactions, subject to the issuer’s risk or fraud control policies, and release any applicable holds on cardholder available funds.

businessRequirements.title: Velocity-processing merchants are advised to send the context-specific SIC Information Code
businessRequirements.requirement: For merchants using velocity processing, the source recommends SIC 5542 for CAT/outside transactions and SIC 5541 for inside transactions; this is a recommendation, not a universal MUST.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: It is recommended for merchants who use velocity processing to send the SIC Information Code (Data Segment 111, Table ID 007) of “5542” for CAT (outside) transactions and “5541” for inside transactions.

businessRequirements.title: Authorization-only reversal supports POS and CAT authorization-only types
businessRequirements.requirement: The supported reversal contexts are POS Authorization Only type 3 and CAT Authorization Only type 5.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: POS Authorization Only (Transaction Type code “3”)

businessRequirements.title: Authorization-only reversal matches original approval and sequence
businessRequirements.requirement: Successful matching requires the original Approval Number and Sequence Number to be present and identical, and Prompt Code S to identify cancellation.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: Element No. 5 (Approval Number)—present in the original transaction—must be present and identical in the Authorization Only Reversal transaction.

businessRequirements.title: AVS request and response data use their specified data segments
businessRequirements.requirement: AVS information is sent in the Variable Information Data Segment and returned in the Additional Information Data Segment alongside the authorization response code.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: The device sends a transaction request to BUYPASS containing the AVS information in the Variable Information Data Segment

businessRequirements.title: AVS result does not override approval; merchant rejection uses purchase reversal
businessRequirements.requirement: BUYPASS processes an approved Purchase/Capture regardless of AVS result; if the merchant rejects due to AVS, the merchant performs a Purchase Reversal.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: BUYPASS processes all Purchase/Capture transactions when the Response Code is an approval, regardless of the AVS information.

businessRequirements.title: Bill-payment, recurring, and installment transactions carry the Variable Information Indicator
businessRequirements.requirement: The optional bill-payment/recurring/installment service is identified by a Variable Information Indicator in Segment 111.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: These transactions must be identified by a Variable Information Indicator located in the Variable Information section of the Variable Information Data Segment (Segment No. 111).

businessRequirements.title: RFID credit-card capture transmits unaltered Track 2 without card contact
businessRequirements.requirement: RFID capture obtains and transmits full, unaltered Track 2 data wirelessly when the card is near the receiver.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: it refers to the capability of a point-of-sale device to capture and transmit full, unaltered Track 2 data from a card without requiring the card to have contact with the point-of-sale device.

businessRequirements.title: RFID receiver presence determines Point-of-Sale Entry Mode on every transaction
businessRequirements.requirement: When an RFID receiver is connected, Point-of-Sale Entry Mode is populated correctly for all transactions, including swiped, manually keyed, and non-RFID-applicable cards.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: Point-of-Sale Entry Mode (Contained in Element No. 113, Variable Information.) on all transactions when an RFID receiver is connected to the point-of-sale device or controller.

businessRequirements.title: Healthcare auto-substantiation supports the documented credit and PIN-debit issuers
businessRequirements.requirement: The service identifies and substantiates medical and OTC purchases for FSA and HRA accounts using the supported issuer/card contexts.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: The Healthcare Auto-Substantiation Service provided by credit card issuers (Amex®, Discover® Network, MasterCard®, Visa®) and PIN debit card issuers, is supported by these specifications.

businessRequirements.title: Eligible healthcare benefit cards are identified by stored nine-digit BINs
businessRequirements.requirement: The POS stores eligible benefit-card BIN information for use when the card is swiped.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: Eligible benefit cards are identified by a 9-digit BIN.

businessRequirements.title: Healthcare partial approval and split tender handle qualified and nonqualified amounts
businessRequirements.requirement: When partial approval is unsupported, the request is fully approved or declined; when partial approval returns, the POS prompts for remaining balance using another payment method for nonqualified items.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: A Split Tender transaction results when a Partial Approval is returned to the POS in the transaction response.

businessRequirements.title: Optional QHP code 890 reports clinical-services amount
businessRequirements.requirement: When clinical services are represented, Product Code 890 reports their total including the source-defined tax/shipping/discount treatment and contributes to Total QHP Amount.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: Optional Code: 890 Identifies the total amount of clinic or other medical services. This amount is included in Total QHP Amount.

businessRequirements.title: Optional QHP code 891 reports dental-services amount
businessRequirements.requirement: When dental services are represented, Product Code 891 reports their total and contributes to Total QHP Amount.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: Optional Code: 891 Identifies the total amount of dental services. This amount is included in Total QHP Amount.

businessRequirements.title: Optional QHP code 892 reports prescription/Rx-only amount
businessRequirements.requirement: When prescription/Rx-only purchases are represented, Product Code 892 reports their total and contributes to Total QHP Amount.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: Optional Code: 892 Identifies the total amount of prescriptions used to gain access to Rx- only purses. This amount is included in the Total QHP Amount.

businessRequirements.title: Optional QHP code 893 reports vision/optical amount
businessRequirements.requirement: When vision/optical purchases are represented, Product Code 893 reports their total and contributes to Total QHP Amount.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: Optional Code: 893 Identifies the total amount of vision care items. This amount is included in Total QHP Amount.

businessRequirements.title: Required QHP code 894 reports total qualified healthcare amount
businessRequirements.requirement: The required Total QHP Amount includes clinical, dental, prescription/Rx, and vision/optical amounts.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: Required Code: 894 Identifies the total QHP amount. This includes all Clinical Services, Dental Services, Prescription/Rx, and Vision/Optical amounts.

businessRequirements.title: Optional QHP code 895 reports co-payment amount
businessRequirements.requirement: When a co-payment amount is represented, Product Code 895 identifies its total.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: Co-Payment Optional Code: 895 Identifies the total amount for co- payments

businessRequirements.title: Optional QHP code 896 reports transit-purchase amount
businessRequirements.requirement: When transit purchases are represented, Product Code 896 identifies their total.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: Transit Optional Code: 896 Identifies the total amount for transit purchases

businessRequirements.title: Healthcare requests include MSDI, Partial Approval Indicator, and Product Code data
businessRequirements.requirement: FSA/HRA transaction requests include Market-Specific Data Indicator in Segment 111, Partial Approval Indicator in Segment 100, and Product Code Segment 102.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: FSA/HRA transaction requests include the following data fields:

businessRequirements.title: Healthcare responses use standard response data without FSA/HRA-specific elements
businessRequirements.requirement: The response contains standard response data; this service defines no additional FSA/HRA-specific response elements.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: There are no data elements specific to FSA/HRA transactions.

businessRequirements.title: Healthcare card processing supports the documented purchase, reversal, return, and timeout types
businessRequirements.requirement: FSA/HRA supports Purchase/Capture, Purchase Reversal, Merchandise Return, and Time-out Reversal.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: Purchase/Capture

businessRequirements.title: Approved healthcare purchases update the card-type totals bucket
businessRequirements.requirement: An approved FSA/HRA Purchase/Capture requires Partial Approval Indicator and Product Code Segment and adds to the card-type totals count and amount.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: The Partial Approval Indicator and Product Code Data Segment fields are required in a FSA/HRA Purchase/Capture transaction.

businessRequirements.title: Healthcare purchase reversal requires the indicator and reverses totals
businessRequirements.requirement: FSA/HRA Purchase Reversal requires Partial Approval Indicator and subtracts approved reversal count and amount from the card-type totals bucket.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: The Partial Approval Indicator is required in a FSA/HRA Purchase Reversal transaction.

businessRequirements.title: Approved healthcare merchandise returns update totals with the source-defined signs
businessRequirements.requirement: An approved Merchandise Return adds to the card-type totals count and subtracts from the amount.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: All approved Merchandise Return transactions are added to the count and subtracted from the amount of the card type totals bucket.

businessRequirements.title: Healthcare timeout reversal requires the indicator and reverses totals
businessRequirements.requirement: FSA/HRA TOR requires Partial Approval Indicator and subtracts approved TOR count and amount from the card-type totals bucket.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: The Partial Approval Indicator is required in a FSA/HRA TOR transaction.

businessRequirements.title: Approved healthcare receipt shows the QHP indicator and subtotal
businessRequirements.requirement: Approved FSA/HRA receipts print the QHP item indicator and subtotal including taxes and discounts, in addition to general credit-card receipt requirements.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: Indicator that identifies the QHP items on the customer receipt

businessRequirements.title: Credit-card receipt prints merchant name and address
businessRequirements.requirement: The merchant's name and address are printed on all credit-card receipts.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: The merchant's name and address prints on all credit card receipts.

businessRequirements.title: Credit-card receipt prints the transaction type
businessRequirements.requirement: The transaction type is printed on every receipt.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: The Transaction Type prints on all receipts.

businessRequirements.title: Credit-card receipt masks the account number to its last four digits
businessRequirements.requirement: The printed account number preserves only the last four digits and uses X characters for the suppressed digits, preserving original field width.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: The Account Number (Element No. 2) must be truncated—suppressed to its last four digits—on all transaction receipts.

businessRequirements.title: Credit-card receipt suppresses the expiration date
businessRequirements.requirement: The presented card expiration date does not appear on transaction receipts.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: The Expiration Date must be suppressed on all transaction receipts.

businessRequirements.title: Credit-card receipt prints the transaction date
businessRequirements.requirement: The transaction date is printed on every credit-card receipt.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: The date of the transaction prints on all credit card receipts.

businessRequirements.title: Credit-card receipt prints the transaction time
businessRequirements.requirement: The transaction time is printed on every credit-card receipt.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: The time of the transaction prints on all credit card receipts.

businessRequirements.title: Credit-card receipt prints the transaction Sequence Number
businessRequirements.requirement: The transaction Sequence Number is printed on every credit-card receipt.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: The transaction's Sequence Number appears on all credit card receipts.

businessRequirements.title: Approved credit receipt prints required fuel product details
businessRequirements.requirement: An approved receipt shows fuel type, quantity in gallons, price per gallon, and total fuel purchase amount.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: Fuel product information

businessRequirements.title: Approved credit receipt prints required nonfuel product details
businessRequirements.requirement: An approved receipt shows number of product units, unit price, and total product purchase amount.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: Nonfuel product information

businessRequirements.title: Receipt prints returned balance for partial approval or balance-return purchase
businessRequirements.requirement: When the issuer returns available balance, it prints for Partial Approval and Balance Return with Purchase on approved or declined receipts.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: Balance information prints on a credit card receipt for a Partial Approval transaction and a Balance Return with Purchase transaction.

businessRequirements.title: Credit-card receipt shows approval code or decline message according to device context
businessRequirements.requirement: Approved POS receipts include the approval phrase and code; declined POS receipts include a decline message when preprint is used; customer-activated devices display the decline message on screen.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: The approval phrase, including the approval code, must be on a receipt for an "approved" transaction that involves a point-of-sale device.

businessRequirements.title: Credit receipt signature line appears only on merchant copy
businessRequirements.requirement: A signature line appears only on the merchant copy of a credit-card transaction receipt.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: A signature line prints only on the merchant’s copy of the credit card transaction receipt.

businessRequirements.title: Credit processing restricts card-read data displayed or stored at point of interaction
businessRequirements.requirement: A device must not display/store card-read data other than account number, expiration date, and cardholder name if present; merchants must not store full magnetic-stripe data.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: A device at the point of interaction must not display/store any card-read data except the card’s account number, card’s expiration date, and cardholder’s name, if present.

businessRequirements.title: Permitted research records are limited and securely maintained
businessRequirements.requirement: For research, only account number, expiration date, and cardholder name may be recorded in the specified files and must be kept securely; full card-read/discretionary data is prohibited.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: The merchant—or any agent representative thereof—may record only the card’s account number, card’s expiration date, and cardholder’s name on paper, microfiche, or an online authorization file, for research purposes at its site.

businessRequirements.title: Credit clearing data is not reconstructed from previously captured full track data
businessRequirements.requirement: Full card-read data is not stored or reused to produce later authorization/clearing data, except for the explicitly stated TransArmor-Verifone exception.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: Card data provided in a clearing transaction must not be the result of previously captured full card-read data.

businessRequirements.title: Regulatory track selection uses the card-specific default and unaltered fallback
businessRequirements.requirement: Track 2 is default when supported, otherwise unaltered Track 1 before manual entry; Amex uses Track 1 by default and unaltered Track 2 fallback.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: The default track that is sent to the host should be Track 2 if the device supports Track 2.

businessRequirements.title: Host card-data format contains only account number and expiration after an equals delimiter
businessRequirements.requirement: For the enumerated credit transaction types, the host message uses account number, '=' delimiter, and four-digit YYMM expiration date with no further Card Discretionary Data after the date.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: The host message should only contain the Account Number, followed by an account delimiter (=), followed by the 4 digit Expiration Date (Storage format – YYMM).

businessRequirements.title: In-flight track retention is temporary and offline transactions send full unaltered tracks
businessRequirements.requirement: Track 2 may be retained in the In Flight Table only while a transaction is in process and is removed when complete; offline transactions send full unaltered Track 1 and Track 2.

sourceEvidence.verbatimExcerpt: Track 2 data is kept in this table while the transaction is in process.

testCases.reviewObjective: For a credit-card transaction, the device validates the expiration date of the presented card.
When Track 2 is supported, the device sends Track 2 by default; if it cannot read Track 2, it sends unaltered Track 1 before manual entry, subject to the Amex-specific rule.
For American Express, the device sends Track 1 by default and sends unaltered Track 2 before manual entry when Track 1 cannot be read.
For an AFD transaction with encrypted TransArmor data, Track 1 is present in the Encryption Block and the Encryption Target identifies Track 1.
An offline-approved Pre-Auth or Sale sends full track data; follow-up transactions use truncated Track 2 or truncated Track 2 facsimile.
After three unsuccessful magnetic-stripe reads, the device prompts for manual Account Number and Expiration Date in MMYY format.
When manual entry is used, an asterisk precedes the Account Number on the receipt and journal.

Point-of-sale credit processing supports the transaction types enumerated in Section 10.1.2, including purchase/capture, reversal, authorization-only, return, timeout reversal, mail/phone, void, balance inquiry, partial approval, and authorization-only reversal.
Customer-activated credit processing supports Purchase/Capture, Authorization Only, Time-out Reversal, Partial Approval, and Authorization Only Reversal.

With Partial Approval Indicator 1, the network response uses Response Code F, provides the approved amount, and prompts payment of the remaining balance; issuer-returned balance is carried in Segment 112.
Partial Approval is supported for POS Purchase, POS Authorization Only, and CAT Authorization Only.

A reversal of a partially approved authorization uses the amount approved in the original response; BUYPASS supports reversal of the partially approved authorization, not a partial reversal of an original transaction.
For a partially approved transaction, the TOR uses the amount requested in the original request and the original request's Sequence Number.
Approved and partially approved authorizations are cleared or reversed; the source gives separate 24-hour card-present and 72-hour card-absent merchant windows.

The issuer immediately processes a matched reversal subject to its risk/fraud controls and releases any applicable hold on cardholder available funds; issuer processing requires independent host/issuer evidence.
For merchants using velocity processing, the source recommends SIC 5542 for CAT/outside transactions and SIC 5541 for inside transactions; this is a recommendation, not a universal MUST.
The supported reversal contexts are POS Authorization Only type 3 and CAT Authorization Only type 5.
Successful matching requires the original Approval Number and Sequence Number to be present and identical, and Prompt Code S to identify cancellation.
AVS information is sent in the Variable Information Data Segment and returned in the Additional Information Data Segment alongside the authorization response code.
BUYPASS processes an approved Purchase/Capture regardless of AVS result; if the merchant rejects due to AVS, the merchant performs a Purchase Reversal.
The optional bill-payment/recurring/installment service is identified by a Variable Information Indicator in Segment 111.
RFID capture obtains and transmits full, unaltered Track 2 data wirelessly when the card is near the receiver.
When an RFID receiver is connected, Point-of-Sale Entry Mode is populated correctly for all transactions, including swiped, manually keyed, and non-RFID-applicable cards.
The service identifies and substantiates medical and OTC purchases for FSA and HRA accounts using the supported issuer/card contexts.
The POS stores eligible benefit-card BIN information for use when the card is swiped.

When partial approval is unsupported, the request is fully approved or declined; when partial approval returns, the POS prompts for remaining balance using another payment method for nonqualified items.
When clinical services are represented, Product Code 890 reports their total including the source-defined tax/shipping/discount treatment and contributes to Total QHP Amount.
When dental services are represented, Product Code 891 reports their total and contributes to Total QHP Amount.
When prescription/Rx-only purchases are represented, Product Code 892 reports their total and contributes to Total QHP Amount.
When vision/optical purchases are represented, Product Code 893 reports their total and contributes to Total QHP Amount.
The required Total QHP Amount includes clinical, dental, prescription/Rx, and vision/optical amounts.
When a co-payment amount is represented, Product Code 895 identifies its total.
When transit purchases are represented, Product Code 896 identifies their total.
FSA/HRA transaction requests include Market-Specific Data Indicator in Segment 111, Partial Approval Indicator in Segment 100, and Product Code Segment 102.
The response contains standard response data; this service defines no additional FSA/HRA-specific response elements.
FSA/HRA supports Purchase/Capture, Purchase Reversal, Merchandise Return, and Time-out Reversal.
An approved FSA/HRA Purchase/Capture requires Partial Approval Indicator and Product Code Segment and adds to the card-type totals count and amount.
FSA/HRA Purchase Reversal requires Partial Approval Indicator and subtracts approved reversal count and amount from the card-type totals bucket.
An approved Merchandise Return adds to the card-type totals count and subtracts from the amount.
FSA/HRA TOR requires Partial Approval Indicator and subtracts approved TOR count and amount from the card-type totals bucket.
Approved FSA/HRA receipts print the QHP item indicator and subtotal including taxes and discounts, in addition to general credit-card receipt requirements.
The merchant's name and address are printed on all credit-card receipts.
The transaction type is printed on every receipt.
The printed account number preserves only the last four digits and uses X characters for the suppressed digits, preserving original field width.
The presented card expiration date does not appear on transaction receipts.
The transaction date is printed on every credit-card receipt.
The transaction time is printed on every credit-card receipt.
The transaction Sequence Number is printed on every credit-card receipt.
An approved receipt shows fuel type, quantity in gallons, price per gallon, and total fuel purchase amount.
An approved receipt shows number of product units, unit price, and total product purchase amount.
When the issuer returns available balance, it prints for Partial Approval and Balance Return with Purchase on approved or declined receipts.
Approved POS receipts include the approval phrase and code; declined POS receipts include a decline message when preprint is used; customer-activated devices display the decline message on screen.
A signature line appears only on the merchant copy of a credit-card transaction receipt.
A device must not display/store card-read data other than account number, expiration date, and cardholder name if present; merchants must not store full magnetic-stripe data.
For research, only account number, expiration date, and cardholder name may be recorded in the specified files and must be kept securely; full card-read/discretionary data is prohibited.
Full card-read data is not stored or reused to produce later authorization/clearing data, except for the explicitly stated TransArmor-Verifone exception.
Track 2 is default when supported, otherwise unaltered Track 1 before manual entry; Amex uses Track 1 by default and unaltered Track 2 fallback.
For the enumerated credit transaction types, the host message uses account number, '=' delimiter, and four-digit YYMM expiration date with no further Card Discretionary Data after the date.
Track 2 may be retained in the In Flight Table only while a transaction is in process and is removed when complete; offline transactions send full unaltered Track 1 and Track 2.
